sources.entry: Core-Monitor - Open-source macOS system monitor with menu bar stats, a full dashboard, optional fan control, and Touch Bar widgets.

summary.one_liner: Core-Monitor is a free, open-source, native macOS system monitor for Apple Silicon Macs that shows hardware stats in the menu bar and dashboard and offers optional fan control.
summary.what_it_does: Shows CPU, GPU, memory, battery, thermals, power draw, fan speeds, network, and disk readings, sourced from the Apple SMC and standard macOS system APIs. The menu bar can display chosen readings, and a compact popover gives a larger summary. The direct-download edition can set fixed or custom-curve fan speeds through an optional privileged helper, which returns fans to automatic control when turned off or when its connection or lease lapses. Live widgets can be placed on the Touch Bar on Macs that have one. Live weather is off by default and, when enabled, uses Apple WeatherKit with macOS location access. A Mac App Store edition is available with a sandboxed, read-only scope.
use_cases: monitor CPU and GPU usage on a Mac
show system stats in the menu bar
control Mac fan speed with a custom curve
view temperatures and power draw on Apple Silicon
add live widgets to the Touch Bar
how_to_run: Download Core-Monitor.app.zip or the .dmg from the latest GitHub release
Or clone the repository and open Core-Monitor.xcodeproj in Xcode
Build and run the Core-Monitor scheme
notable: Fan control through a privileged helper that sends heartbeats and reverts fans to automatic control if the connection drops
Two editions: full direct download with SMC sensors versus sandboxed App Store edition
No account, no ads, no analytics; monitoring data stays local
Weather via Apple WeatherKit is opt-in and the developer does not receive that data
caveats: Requires macOS 13 or later on an Apple Silicon Mac
Fan control and Touch Bar widgets are not available in the Mac App Store edition
The helper must be reinstalled when updating; README notes hardware-test and compatibility limits on a separate page
